---
title: "EnerHabitat"
subtitle: "Thermal simulation of opaque constructive systems (walls and roofs) from EPW data — 1D and 2D"
---

**EnerHabitat** is a Python package for the thermal simulation of opaque constructive
systems (walls and roofs) driven by EPW weather data. It solves the time-dependent heat
conduction equation across multi-layer systems — in **1D** for homogeneous layers
(`System`) and in **2D** for units that are heterogeneous across their width, such as
concrete hollow-block walls and joist-and-block (*vigueta y bovedilla*) roofs
(`System2D`) — and produces indoor temperatures and air-conditioning energy demands for
an *average day* of a chosen month [@barrios2016].

The model considers a single opaque envelope component: no windows, no ventilation, no
infiltration, no internal gains — so any difference in the results is caused by the
constructive system alone. Two solution modes are available: **free-running** (the
indoor temperature evolves with the system's dynamics) and **air-conditioned** (the
indoor temperature is held at a comfort setpoint and the energy demands are reported).

## Installation

```bash
pip install enerhabitat        # or: uv add enerhabitat
```

Requires **Python ≥ 3.10**. The section inspector plots are an optional extra:
`pip install enerhabitat[viz]`.

## Quickstart

EnerHabitat ships **no** materials: create a `materials.ini` in your working directory
(or point `eh.config.file` to one) before running anything:

```ini
[Adobe]
k   = 0.58    # W/(m·K)
rho = 1500    # kg/m³
c   = 1480    # J/(kg·K)
```

```python
import enerhabitat as eh

eh.config.file = "./materials.ini"           # 1) materials (required)
loc = eh.Location("./epw/example.epw")       # 2) location from an EPW

wall = eh.System(location=loc)               # 3) constructive system
wall.azimuth = 90                            #    east-facing wall
wall.absortance = 0.3
wall.layers = [("Adobe", 0.20)]              #    outside → inside

loc.meanDay(month=5, year=2025)              # 4) average day of May
wall.Tsa()                                   #    sun–air temperature

ti = wall.solve()                            # 5) free-running indoor temperature
print(wall.energy_transfer)                  #    J/(m²·day)
```
